correctness.rationale: Complete face enumeration is finite because every selected arc meets one of the two central vertices, each with at most one incoming/outgoing arc, bounding the face size at four. The exact augmented face counts are 115,313,711,1417 for n=3,4,5,6. Sequential arc-type toggling pairs respectively 54,152,339,624 faces with disjoint cofaces; topological sorting of all 288,896,2200,4608 oriented Hasse incidences proves acyclicity. One empty-face match yields an ordinary Morse model with a single vertex. Independent integral signed chain cancellations confirm the critical-cell dimensions and boundary matrices (1x6 zero; 8x1 content 2; 1x32 content 2; 0x169 zero). Hurewicz/degree classification of attaching maps to S^1 or wedges of S^2 and unimodular changes yield the four actual homotopy types, not just homology. The unstable dynamical-module assertion follows from directed 2-/4-cycle closure of any contained arc and positive in/outdegrees. Both standalone programs executed successfully after copies were inspected.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating article deals with bidirected path and polygon hosts and establishes their homology/partial homotopy, whereas this work classifies bidirected complete bipartite hosts with torsion. The 2022 paper studies its complete bipartite digraph with one-way orientation, §3.2, and hence only the chessboard complex; its introduction explicitly conjectures that torsion of a dynamical module implies stability, which these newly calculated unstable modules contradict. The 2024 weak categorical quiver-minor paper proves genus-bounded torsion existence/bounds and a matching-complex equivalence only for digraphs without oriented cycles; it does not determine these complexes. Record searches of graph Morse complexes and higher matching complexes have different face definitions and do not dominate the statement. The searches were source-, object-, parameter-, alias-, and reduction-aware, and no explicit published equivalent or stronger covering theorem was identified. Absolute priority is not claimed.
residual_risks: Unindexed, later or unpublished computations could yield equivalent homotopy decompositions, so absence in searched sources does not certify priority.
Theoretical papers on other complexes can contain embedded examples outside title/abstract indexing; inspected the most plausible primary full texts but cannot certify exhaustive worldwide coverage.
The n=3..6 classification does not establish persistence, absence, or periodicity of two-torsion beyond n=6.

RESULT.md: finite exact homotopy classifications and uniform module lemma
value.rationale: Bidirected complete bipartite hosts are a canonical highly symmetric next family after the newly studied bidirected paths and polygons. The first four nonpolygonal widths reveal a mathematically meaningful transition: torsion-free wedge, then mod-two Moore summands in two successive widths, then a pure high-dimensional wedge. The exact CW attaching degrees isolate the unstable homotopy obstruction and yield precise integral homotopy types that Betti numbers alone cannot establish. Most importantly, a short uniform directed-cycle lemma makes the two torsion-bearing hosts unstable dynamical modules, directly negating a specific stated torsion-implies-stability conjecture. This supplies genuine conceptual significance for otherwise finite classifications. No paper-sized or all-width theorem is claimed.
risks: Does not classify larger complete-bipartite widths
The 2026 polygon conjecture is a distinct statement and is not affected
